items.followUp: A 2 kg body moves at 6 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.

accept: energy possessed by a body due to its motion
rubric.why: Awards the mark for the definition of kinetic energy.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy in terms of a body's motion.
rubric.how: State that kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses because it is moving.

rubric.why: Work done is the starting point of the derivation.
rubric.description: Uses the equation for work done.

rubric.why: Relates the distance travelled to the speed for a body starting from rest.
rubric.description: Uses the equation of motion with initial speed zero.
rubric.how: Write v² = 2as and rearrange to find s.

rubric.why: Shows the substitution into work and the resulting kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.description: Substitutes F = ma and the expression for s into W = Fs to obtain the equation for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Show the substitution and state KE = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
For a body starting from rest, the work done is W = Fs.
Using the equation of motion, v² = 2as, so s = v²/(2a).
Since F = ma, KE = W = ma × v²/(2a) = 1/2 mv².

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts perpendicularly at a distance of 0.25 m from a pivot. Find the torque.

rubric.why: Recognises the given force and converts the lever arm to SI units.
rubric.description: Records the force and the perpendicular distance in metres.
rubric.how: Write F = 100 N and convert 10 cm to 0.10 m.

rubric.why: Uses the torque relation for a perpendicular force.
Shows correct substitution of the SI values.
rubric.description: Substitutes the force and perpendicular distance.

rubric.why: Awards the marks for the correct torque value and unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the torque and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Evaluate the product and state the answer in N m.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 100 N and d = 10 cm = 0.10 m; the force acts perpendicularly.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N acts on an area of 2.0 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Identifies the force and contact area from the question.
rubric.description: Records the given force and area.
rubric.how: Write F = 75 N and A = 1.5 cm².

rubric.why: Pressure must be calculated using area in SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the contact area to square metres.

rubric.why: Awards the marks for the correct calculated pressure and unit.
rubric.how: Substitute the SI values, evaluate, and state the answer in Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 75 N, A = 1.5 cm² = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m².

items.followUp: Give one example each of a base unit and a derived unit.

rubric.why: Identifies base units as independent fundamental units.
rubric.description: Defines base units or gives suitable examples.
rubric.how: State that base units are independent fundamental units, or name examples such as metre, kilogram and second.

rubric.why: Identifies derived units as combinations of base units.
rubric.description: Defines derived units or gives a suitable example.
rubric.how: State that derived units are formed by combining base units, or give an example such as m/s or the newton.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent fundamental units, such as the metre, kilogram and second.
Derived units are formed by combining base units, such as m/s or the newton (kg m/s²).

items.followUp: Define position and state the position of an object using a suitable reference point.

accept: location of an object relative to a reference point
location of an object relative to an origin
position relative to a reference point
rubric.why: Position is specified with respect to a reference point or origin.
rubric.description: Defines position relative to a reference point.
rubric.how: State that position is the location of an object relative to a reference point.

rubric.why: Awards the mark for a clear example of position relative to a reference.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of an object's position.
rubric.how: For example, state that a student is 5 m east of a pole.

modelAnswer: Position is the location of an object relative to a reference point.
For example, a student may be 5 m east of a pole.
